claims.text: The technical people trying to control agents for real are reaching for hooks: small programs the agent's harness runs at fixed points, before and after a tool call, when a prompt is submitted, when the agent stops.
claims.quote: small programs the agent's harness runs at fixed points, before a tool call, after it, when a prompt is submitted, when the agent stops

claims.text: The design has converged: at least ten agent tools, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, Devin Desktop, Grok Build, Factory, Augment and Kiro, document a hook before a tool call that can block it.
claims.quote: At least ten agent tools document a hook before a tool call that can block it

value.unit: agent tools with a blocking pre-tool hook, at least

claims.text: The tools differ where it matters for security: whether an organisation can force its own hooks, whether a failing hook blocks or lets the action through, whether repository hooks need trust, and whether anything sees the model's output.
claims.quote: The design has converged; the security properties have not.

claims.text: A hook is a program the agent's harness runs at a fixed point in its loop, with the event on its input and a decision on its output; the pre-tool hook sees the tool and its full input and can allow, deny, ask or rewrite.
claims.quote: A hook is a program the agent's harness runs at a fixed point in its loop

claims.text: Claude Code's reference lists 33 events from session start to configuration changes; most tools have ten to twenty, and on most, exit code 2 blocks.
claims.quote: lists 33 events, from session start to configuration changes

value.unit: hook events in Claude Code's reference

claims.text: This site already runs on hooks: one prints the agent's written policy back after every summary, and another appends the status report at the end of its answers.
claims.quote: This site already runs on them.

claims.text: Anthropic has the richest surface, an allowManagedHooksOnly setting, and since version 2.1.295 an onFailure block option, because a policy hook with a wrong path or a crashing script lets everything through.
claims.quote: a policy hook with a wrong path or a crashing script lets everything through

claims.text: Codex has hooks with a managed-only option, hosted tools such as web search not covered, and docs that call hooks a useful guardrail, not a complete enforcement boundary; ChatGPT has admin controls rather than hooks.
claims.quote: Treat tool hooks as a useful guardrail, not a complete enforcement boundary.

claims.text: Gemini CLI is the only coding agent with documented hooks around the model call itself, BeforeModel and AfterModel, and it warns that project-level hooks are risky when opening untrusted projects.
claims.quote: The only coding agent with documented hooks around the model call itself

claims.text: GitHub Copilot lets organisations install machine-wide policy hooks that load before all others, but command hook timeouts are always fail-open, even for admin-deployed policy hooks.
claims.quote: Command hook timeouts are always fail-open, even for preToolUse and admin-deployed policy hooks.

claims.text: Cursor has hooks at four levels, Enterprise, Team, Project and User; crashes, timeouts and exit codes other than 2 fail open by default, with a failClosed option recommended for MCP hooks.
claims.quote: Crashes, timeouts, and non-zero exit codes other than 2 fail open by default

claims.text: On most tools a hook that crashes, times out or returns something malformed lets the action through; a security hook with a bug is no hook at all unless fail closed is set.
claims.quote: A security hook with a bug is no hook at all

claims.text: Hooks only see what is routed through them: Anthropic's tracker has a case where a hook blocked an edit and the agent made the change through a tool the hook did not cover, closed not planned.
claims.quote: the agent made the change through a different tool the hook did not cover

claims.text: Hooks run with the user's full permissions beside an agent with the same, so unless installed where the agent cannot write, the agent can change the files that define them.
claims.quote: execute shell commands with your full user permissions

claims.text: Hooks shipped in a repository are an attack surface: Check Point's Caught in the Hook, 25 February 2026, found hook commands in project settings ran automatically without confirmation, since patched.
claims.quote: hook commands defined in .claude/settings.json will run automatically without confirmation

claims.text: Before version 3.0.0 Cursor could execute workspace-defined Claude hook commands without approval, fixed in June 2026, and a September 2026 paper on attacker-controlled hook updates compromised all seven harnesses it evaluated.
claims.quote: could execute workspace-defined Claude hook commands

value.unit: harnesses compromised by attacker-controlled hook updates

claims.text: In a headless or SDK run Claude Code never shows the trust dialog and treats the folder as trusted, so a repository's hooks run unreviewed; and most hooks cannot see the model's output.
claims.quote: treats the folder as trusted

claims.text: The people who build hook collections agree: Trail of Bits says hooks are not a security boundary, guardrails not walls, and cc-safety-net says it is not a sandbox and a broken config never blocks anything.
claims.quote: The people who build hook collections agree.

claims.text: In a throwaway repository a project-level hook implementing one rule of the site's policy stopped a push to a disallowed remote in a real headless run, and asked to try other ways the agent declined.
claims.quote: the hook stopped the push to the other remote, and nothing arrived there

claims.text: Run directly, the same hook let through a command whose text did not show where it would push, the limit of any hook that reads text rather than effects.
claims.quote: which is the limit of any hook that reads text rather than effects

claims.text: The headless run also loaded the owner's user-level hooks, because hooks follow the user, and a status counter that reads command text counted the throwaway commit as the site's.
claims.quote: a hook that infers behaviour from text cannot tell one repository from another

claims.text: As a defender: make the organisation's hooks the only hooks, fail closed, hook every path to the same effect, watch the configuration, review repository settings before a headless run, and pair hooks with a boundary.
claims.quote: Hooks decide; the boundary holds.

claims.text: OWASP's GenAI Security Project hosts the Agent Control Standard, built on declarative hooks: a separate guardian answers allow, deny, modify, ask or defer, using policy engines such as OPA or Cedar.
claims.quote: a separate guardian inspects what an agent is about to do, and answers with allow, deny, modify, ask or defer

claims.text: No cross-vendor specification is yet how the major coding agents expose their hooks, which is why the same hook still has to be written several times.
claims.quote: which is why the same hook still has to be written several times

claims.text: The map is from documentation read on 14 October 2026, partly by research agents; the quoted claims were re-checked and the cells marked unknown were not verified.
claims.quote: The map is from documentation.

claims.text: Products move fast: several of these hook systems are months old and change release by release.
claims.quote: Several of these hook systems are months old and their behaviour is changing release by release.

claims.text: The test was one check in one tool; it shows a hook enforcing a rule and its limit, not a measure of any product's security.
claims.quote: The test was one check in one tool.

claims.text: The failure modes are described, not demonstrated; the sources are cited for anyone who needs the detail.
claims.quote: Failure modes are described, not demonstrated.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 14 October 2026, written by the site's agent; four research agents read each vendor's documentation the same day, with the quoted claims re-checked.
claims.quote: The research was done the same day by four research agents reading each vendor's documentation
